newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice export prices seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice export prices seen easing.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to ease next week on low purchases by foreign buyers, though IRRI-6 could firm dealers said Thursday.

Sluggish export orders were likely to depress prices of super, ordinary and kernal varieties of basmati rice, but demand from the Gulf and African countries could lead to higher prices for IRRI-6, a cheaper variety, one exporter said.
An official of the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said it was in contact with buyers in the Philippines and expected to reach a deal. He gave no details.
The TCP, which sold some 40,000 tonnes of rice to Mauritius early this month, was also contacting other major importers in the Gulf and African countries, the official said.
Pakistan exported 1.004 million tonnes of rice worth $279 million in the first eight months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) against 828,000 worth $277 million in the year-ago period.
In February rice exports rose to 192,976 tonnes worth $47 million compared to 142,317 tonnes worth $36 million in January and 123,707 worth $40 million in February 1996.
